Repo: /home/mudathir/all/cvc5/mudathir (cvc5, branch lazy). Uncommitted changes: run
"git diff" there. New feature: option arith-liastar-main-solver moves the lazy LIA* cell
enumeration from a per-lambda subsolver into the MAIN solver. Design (see MainEnum in
src/theory/arith/liastar/liastar_extension.h and mainSolverCheckStar/advanceStage/
emitDriverLemma/getModelDisjunct/getMainEnum/addEnumLemma in liastar_extension.cpp):
- lambda bound vars -> fresh integer skolems y; base(y) = predicate (ites/nots removed) + y>=0.
- Stage guards: h_0 => base(y); per discovered cone-disjunct D_k a fresh h_k with
  h_k => h_{k-1} and h_k => not(D_k(y)); en.guard is the current h_k; each h is
  ensureLiteral'd and preferPhase'd true. h_0 additionally gets a split lemma.
- Driver lemma per (literal, stage): literal => (p[v] or star_k or h_k), unguarded,
  where star_k = d_lastStarLia[literal] (under-approximation built by processDisjunct)
  and p[v] is the vector predicate. Claimed satisfiability-preserving.
- Each full-effort round: catch up stages for cones discovered via other literals; if
  guard fixed false at level 0 (Valuation::isFixed) -> emit exact equivalence
  (processDisjunct complete=true); if guard true in SAT assignment -> read the cell from
  arithModel via getModelDisjunct (substitute+rewrite each atom of base; equality atoms
  false in model become strict inequalities; skolems missing from arithModel fall back to
  TheoryArith::getCandidateModelValue), dedupe against d_lazyCones, advanceStage, then
  processDisjunct(false) emits the guarded equivalence g_k => (literal = star_k) and
  deactivates the previous g; then emitDriverLemma for the new stage.
- Tests: all 9 regress1/arith/liastar tests pass in this mode (Debug), and in the other
  three modes (accumulate/push-pop/eager); unit test passes.
Focus ONLY on problems introduced by the new main-solver mode (not pre-existing issues in
the subsolver paths). Report findings with concrete code references.
A reviewer (lens mechanics) claims:
Title: MainEnum state outlives user-context-scoped lemmas: wrong sat after pop in incremental mode (confirmed)
Detail: All guard-chain lemmas (h_0 => base, h_k => h_{k-1}, h_k => not(D_k), drivers) are sent as ordinary theory lemmas and are RETRACTED on user-context pop, but the bookkeeping that gates their emission lives in non-context-dependent std::maps: d_mainEnums and d_lastDriver (src/theory/arith/liastar/liastar_extension.h:450-462), plus en.negated and en.guard inside MainEnum. getMainEnum only seeds h_0 => base once per lambda lifetime (liastar_extension.cpp:823-884), advanceStage lemmas are emitted once per cone (en.negated never resets), and emitDriverLemma no-ops when d_lastDriver[literal] == en.guard. After a pop, en.guard refers to a dangling SAT variable with no chain behind it: the SAT solver can set it true while the skolems sit in an already-covered cell; mainSolverCheckStar then re-harvests a known cell, the dedupe path (liastar_extension.cpp:1118-1128) re-emits an already-cached driver, doPendingLemmas sends nothing, and the candidate model is accepted. CONFIRMED: /tmp/liastar_pushpop2.smt2 (check (1 1) unsat, pop, then check (2 1) with the same lambda, which is also unsat since 2+1 < 5) answers `unsat` then `sat` in main-solver mode; subsolver mode answers `unsat`/`unsat`. The subsolver mode is immune because its accumulated state lives in the subsolver, not in the main SAT solver's retractable clause database. Note the existing regress test simple.smt2 uses push/pop but masks this because its second query is certified via the p[v] split. Fix direction: make the per-lambda/per-literal gating user-context-dependent (CDO/CDHashMap on userContext()), or re-seed the full chain when the user context changes.
Adversarially verify against the actual code (git diff + files). Is this a REAL problem
introduced by the new main-solver mode? Default isReal=false unless the reasoning reproduces
concretely from the code.

- deep-research: Deep research harness — fan-out web searches, fetch sources, adversarially verify claims, synthesize a cited report. - When the user wants a deep, multi-source, fact-checked research report on any topic. BEFORE invoking, check if the question is specific enough to research directly — if underspecified (e.g., "what car to buy" without budget/use-case/region), ask 2-3 clarifying questions to narrow scope. Then pass the refined question as args, weaving the answers in.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- verify: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by running the app and observing behavior. Use when asked to verify a PR, confirm a fix works, test a change manually, check that a feature works, or validate local changes before pushing.
- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a pull request
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

11	 * ****************************************************************************
12	 *
13	 * Extension to the theory of arithmetic handling the lia* (LIA star) operator.
14	 */
15	
16	#ifdef CVC5_USE_NORMALIZ
17	
18	#ifndef CVC5__THEORY__ARITH__LIASTAR_EXTENSION_H
19	#define CVC5__THEORY__ARITH__LIASTAR_EXTENSION_H
20	
21	#include <map>
22	#include <memory>
23	#include <vector>
24	
25	#include "expr/node.h"
26	#include "libnormaliz/libnormaliz.h"
27	#include "smt/env_obj.h"
28	#include "smt/solver_engine.h"
29	#include "theory/arith/liastar/liastar_proof_generator.h"
30	#include "theory/ext_theory.h"
31	#include "theory/theory.h"
32	
33	namespace cvc5::internal {
34	namespace theory {
35	namespace arith {
36	
37	class InferenceManager;
38	class TheoryArith;
39	
40	namespace liastar {
41	
42	/** Arbitrary-precision integers (the integer type handed to Normaliz). */
43	typedef mpz_class Integer;
44	/** A row of arithmetic terms, e.g. the monomials of one cone contribution. */
45	typedef std::vector<Node> Vector;
46	
47	/**
48	 * Extension to TheoryArith deciding the lia* operator STAR_CONTAINS.
49	 *
50	 * A literal
51	 *     (int.star-contains (lambda ((x_1 Int) ... (x_n Int)) p) v_1 ... v_n)
52	 * asserts that the vector v = (v_1, ..., v_n) belongs to the additive closure
53	 * (the *star*) of the set S = { x in Z^n : p(x), x >= 0 }, i.e. that v is a
54	 * finite sum of vectors each satisfying p. The extension decides such literals
55	 * by reducing them to plain linear integer arithmetic, following
56	 *
57	 * - Levatich, M., Bjorner, N., Piskac, R., Shoham, S. (2020).
58	 *   Solving LIA* Using Approximations.
59	 *   VMCAI 2020.
60	 *   https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-030-39322-9_17
61	 *
62	 * The reduction views each convex cell (DNF disjunct) of p as a polyhedral
63	 * cone, computes the cone's Hilbert basis and module generators with Normaliz,
64	 * and encodes the star of the union of cells as a system of linear constraints
65	 * over fresh non-negative multipliers (the "star constraints"). The reduction
66	 * lemma `literal = star` is sent through TheoryArith's inference manager. See
67	 * the file comment of liastar_extension.cpp for the full picture.
68	 *
69	 * The main entry point is checkFullEffort(...), called by TheoryArith at
70	 * full/last-call effort with the current candidate arithmetic model. Two
71	 * strategies are available (option arith-lia-star-lazy):
72	 * - eager (`eagerCheckStar`): normalize p to DNF and reduce in one shot;
73	 * - lazy (`lazyCheckStar`): discover one convex cell per refinement round from
74	 *   models of a persistent incremental subsolver, asserting guarded
75	 *   under-approximations until every cell is covered.
76	 */
77	class LiaStarExtension : EnvObj
78	{
79	 public:
80	  LiaStarExtension(Env& env, TheoryArith& containing);
81	  ~LiaStarExtension();
82	
83	  /**
84	   * Does non-context dependent setup for a node connected to a theory:
85	   * registers STAR_CONTAINS terms with the extended theory and records that
86	   * this extension has work to do.
87	   */
88	  void preRegisterTerm(TNode n);
89	
90	  /**
91	   * Performs the main checks for liastar arithmetic, based on the current
92	   * (linear) arithmetic model from `arithModel`. This method may already send
93	   * lemmas, but most lemmas are buffered and sent at LAST_CALL effort by
94	   * TheoryArith. The motivation for this strategy is to allow other
95	   * non-terminating theories (e.g. quantifiers, strings) to run full effort
96	   * checks, before sending the lemmas generated by liastar.
97	   *
98	   * For each STAR_CONTAINS assertion this emits a non-negativity lemma and a
99	   * split on the substituted predicate p[v], and then -- unless the current
100	   * model already satisfies the literal -- reduces the literal via the eager
101	   * or lazy strategy.
102	   *
103	   * @param arithModel a map of the form { v1 -> c1, ..., vn -> cn } which
104	   *   represents the linear arithmetic theory solver's contribution to the
105	   *   current candidate model, where v1, ..., vn are arithmetic variables and
106	   *   c1, ..., cn are constants
107	   * @param termSet the set of terms relevant in the current check
108	   */
109	  void checkFullEffort(std::map<Node, Node>& arithModel,
110	                       const std::set<Node>& termSet);
111	
112	  /** Does this class need a call to check(...) at last call effort? */
113	  bool hasLiaStarTerms() const { return d_hasLiaStarTerms; }
114	
115	 private:
116	  /**
117	   * Collect from TheoryArith's fact queue the STAR_CONTAINS atoms asserted in
118	   * the current context. Both polarities are reduced to the positive atom:
119	   * the reduction lemma `atom = star` handles either polarity (the
120	   * surrounding SAT solver applies the negation).
121	   */
122	  void getAssertions(std::vector<Node>& assertions);
123	
124	  /**
125	   * Normalize the body p of the lambda `n` into DNF and render each disjunct
126	   * as a Normaliz constraint matrix (see `LiaStarUtils::getMatrices`).
127	   *
128	   * @param n a lambda (lambda ((x_1 Int) ... (x_n Int)) p) with p in QF_LIA
129	   * @return one (constraint rows, disjunct node) pair per DNF disjunct of p,
130	   *   i.e. one per cone
131	   */
132	  const std::vector<std::pair<std::vector<std::string>, Node>>
133	  convertQFLIAToMatrices(Node n);
134	
135	  /**
136	   * Eager path: build a Normaliz cone for every DNF disjunct of the predicate
137	   * and accumulate the star constraints over all of them. Empty (infeasible)
138	   * cones are skipped.
139	   *
140	   * @param n the STAR_CONTAINS literal; its children after the lambda are the
141	   *   vector v
142	   * @param pairs one (constraint rows, disjunct node) pair per disjunct, as
143	   *   returned by `convertQFLIAToMatrices`
144	   * @return the non-empty cones, each paired with the disjunct it came from
145	   *   (used by `getMembershipDisjuncts` for the debug trace), and the star
146	   *   constraints: fresh multiplier skolems with their side constraints plus
147	   *   the sum constraints tying v to the cones' contributions. Their
148	   *   conjunction is equivalent to `v in S*`.
149	   */
150	  std::pair<std::vector<std::pair<Node, libnormaliz::Cone<Integer>>>,
151	            std::vector<Node>>
152	  getCones(Node n,
153	           const std::vector<std::pair<std::vector<std::string>, Node>>& pairs);
154	
155	  /**
156	   * Lazy path: build the cone for a single disjunct and append it to the list
157	   * of cones for `n[0]` (the lambda) stored in `d_lazyCones`. If the cone is
158	   * empty (the disjunct is infeasible) it is not added.
159	   *
160	   * @param n the STAR_CONTAINS literal
161	   * @param pair the disjunct's constraint rows and node, as returned by
162	   *   `LiaStarUtils::getMatrix`
163	   */
164	  void addCone(Node n, const std::pair<std::vector<std::string>, Node>& pair);
165	
166	  /**
167	   * Lazy path: return the star constraints over all cones accumulated so far
168	   * in `d_lazyCones[n[0]]` (the cones added by previous calls to `addCone`).
169	   *
170	   * The per-cone constraints (and their fresh skolems) are computed only for
171	   * cones that have not been processed in a previous call and are accumulated
172	   * in `d_starConstraints[n[0]]`, so the skolems stay stable across refinement
173	   * rounds; the sum constraints, which span all cones, are rebuilt from the
174	   * accumulated `d_lambdas[n[0]]` on each call.
175	   */
176	  std::vector<Node> getStarConstraints(Node n);
177	
178	  /**
179	   * Debug helper, used only for the "liastar-ext-smt" trace. Builds the
180	   * *membership* encoding `v in S`: one existentially quantified formula per
181	   * (cone, module generator) stating that v is the single element
182	   * `g + sum_j l_j h_j` of that cone. The disjunction of all returned
183	   * formulas is equivalent to the predicate itself, which the emitted trace
184	   * queries let an external solver verify.
185	   *
186	   * @param n the STAR_CONTAINS literal
187	   * @param cones the cones with their originating disjuncts, as returned by
188	   *   `getCones`
189	   * @return each membership formula paired with the disjunct it encodes
190	   */
191	  std::vector<std::pair<Node, Node>> getMembershipDisjuncts(
192	      Node n, std::vector<std::pair<Node, libnormaliz::Cone<Integer>>>& cones);
193	
194	  /**
195	   * Performs the eager Hilbert-basis reduction for a single STAR_CONTAINS
196	   * literal. Generates the star reduction lemma equating `literal` with the
197	   * conjunction of star constraints derived from the cones of `lambda`
198	   * (== literal[0]), and sends it via the inference manager. Does nothing if
199	   * the literal has already been processed.
200	   */
201	  void eagerCheckStar(Node literal, Node lambda);
202	
203	  /**
204	   * Performs one round of the lazy Hilbert-basis reduction for a single
205	   * STAR_CONTAINS literal: refines the literal's subsolver with the negations
206	   * of the cone-disjuncts discovered since the previous round, then delegates
207	   * to `lazyHilbert`. Does nothing if the literal has been fully reduced.
208	   */
209	  void lazyCheckStar(Node literal, Node lambda);
210	
211	  /**
212	   * A persistent, incremental subsolver dedicated to one lambda (one
213	   * STAR_CONTAINS predicate). It is used to enumerate the convex cells of the
214	   * predicate's satisfying region: it is seeded once with the (nonnegative)
215	   * predicate at the base user level and then refined across rounds with the
216	   * negations of the discovered cone-disjuncts, either one assertion per
217	   * disjunct (the default) or as a single cumulative refined formula under
218	   * push/pop (option arith-liastar-push-pop); see `lazyCheckStar`.
219	   */
220	  struct Subsolver
221	  {
222	    /** the incremental QF_LIA subsolver. */
223	    std::unique_ptr<SolverEngine> engine;
224	    /** the lambda's bound variables ... */
225	    std::vector<Node> from;
226	    /** ... and the fresh skolem constants substituted for them, since a
227	     * subsolver cannot be given a formula with free (bound) variables. */
228	    std::vector<Node> to;
229	    /**
230	     * The (nonnegative) predicate in skolem space. It is already asserted in
231	     * `engine` at the base user level (so it survives every pop); it is kept
232	     * only to read off the predicate's atoms when building a disjunct from
233	     * the model.
234	     */
235	    Node base;
236	    /**
237	     * Push/pop strategy only: the union (disjunction), in skolem space, of
238	     * the cone-disjuncts discovered so far. Its negation is the refined
239	     * formula currently asserted in `engine`.
240	     */
241	    Node covered;
242	    /** Push/pop strategy only: whether a refined formula is currently
243	     * asserted, i.e. whether `engine` has a pushed frame to pop before
244	     * asserting the next refined formula. */
245	    bool pushed = false;
246	    /** number of cones in `d_lazyCones[lambda]` already negated in `engine`
247	     * (or, for the push/pop strategy, folded into `covered`). */
248	    size_t negated = 0;
249	  };
250	
251	  /**
252	   * Returns the subsolver for `lambda`, creating and seeding it (with the
253	   * nonnegative predicate) on first use.
254	   */
255	  Subsolver& getSubsolver(Node lambda);
256	
257	  /**
258	   * One lazy refinement round for `literal`: ask the subsolver for a model in
259	   * a region of the predicate not yet covered by a cone, read off the convex
260	   * cell containing it (`LiaStarUtils::getDisjunct`), and hand it to
261	   * `processDisjunct`.
262	   */
263	  void lazyHilbert(Node literal, Subsolver& sub);
264	
265	  /**
266	   * Shared tail of one lazy refinement round (used by both the subsolver and
267	   * the main-solver enumeration): turn `disjunct` -- a freshly discovered
268	   * cell of the predicate, in bound-variable space -- into a cone, rebuild
269	   * the star constraints over all cones found so far, and emit the reduction
270	   * lemma: guarded by a fresh boolean while the star is still an
271	   * under-approximation (`complete` false), unconditional once every cell is
272	   * covered (`complete` true, `disjunct` is then the false constraint).
273	   */
274	  void processDisjunct(Node literal, Node disjunct, bool complete);
275	
276	  /**
277	   * State for enumerating the convex cells of one lambda's predicate in the
278	   * main solver (option arith-liastar-main-solver), replacing the dedicated
279	   * subsolver. The lambda's bound variables are replaced by fresh skolems
280	   * (`from` -> `to`) that live in the main solver, constrained through a
281	   * chain of stage guards: h_0 => base, and for every discovered
282	   * cone-disjunct D_k a fresh h_k with h_k => h_{k-1} and h_k => not(D_k)
283	   * (two constant-size lemmas per stage, accumulate style). The current
284	   * stage guard h_k therefore activates `base and not(D_1) ... and not(D_k)`,
285	   * i.e. it places the skolems in a cell not yet covered by a cone; the cell
286	   * is then read off the main solver's candidate arithmetic model.
287	   *
288	   * The enumeration is driven by the literal itself: each stage emits the
289	   * (satisfiability-preserving) driver lemma
290	   *     literal => (p[v] or star_k or h_k),
291	   * so a model that claims the literal without certifying it must activate
292	   * h_k and thereby exhibit a fresh cell; once every cell is covered the h_k
293	   * branch closes by conflict and the driver leaves exactly the certified
294	   * branches. Completeness is additionally detected when the SAT solver
295	   * fixes the stage guard false at level 0 (`Valuation::isFixed`), at which
296	   * point the exact reduction is emitted.
297	   */
298	  struct MainEnum
299	  {
300	    /** the lambda's bound variables ... */
301	    std::vector<Node> from;
302	    /** ... and the fresh skolems substituted for them in the main solver. */
303	    std::vector<Node> to;
304	    /** The (nonnegative) predicate in skolem space. It is asserted under the
305	     * first stage guard; it is also used to read off the predicate's atoms
306	     * when building a disjunct from the model. */
307	    Node base;
308	    /** The current stage guard h_k (a decision variable, biased true). */
309	    Node guard;
310	    /** number of cones in `d_lazyCones[lambda]` already negated via stage
311	     * guards. */
312	    size_t negated = 0;
313	  };
314	
315	  /**
316	   * Returns the main-solver enumeration state for `lambda`, creating it (and
317	   * queueing its seed lemmas: the guard split and `guard => base`) on first
318	   * use.
319	   */
320	  MainEnum& getMainEnum(Node lambda);
321	
322	  /**
323	   * One refinement round of the main-solver lazy strategy for `literal`:
324	   * depending on the guard's value in the current SAT assignment, read a
325	   * fresh cell from the candidate model (guard true), conclude completeness
326	   * (guard fixed false), or bias the guard and wait (otherwise). See
327	   * `MainEnum`.
328	   */
329	  void mainSolverCheckStar(Node literal,
330	                           Node lambda,
331	                           const std::map<Node, Node>& arithModel);
332	
333	  /**
334	   * Read the cell of `en.base` containing the current candidate arithmetic
335	   * model: fix the truth value of every atom of `en.base` under `arithModel`
336	   * (consulting `TheoryArith::getCandidateModelValue` for skolems missing
337	   * from the map) and return the conjunction in bound-variable space.
338	   * Returns the null node if some atom cannot be evaluated to a constant.
339	   */
340	  Node getModelDisjunct(MainEnum& en, const std::map<Node, Node>& arithModel);
341	
342	  /**
343	   * Queue a main-solver enumeration lemma (InferenceId ARITH_LIA_STAR_ENUM),
344	   * skipping lemmas that rewrite to a constant.
345	   */
346	  void addEnumLemma(Node lemma);
347	
348	  /**
349	   * Open a new enumeration stage for `en`: a fresh guard that activates the
350	   * previous stage's constraints plus the negation of the newly covered

388	   * further lemmas are generated for these.

390	  std::vector<Node> d_processedStarTerms;
391	
392	  /**
393	   * The cones accumulated so far during the lazy Hilbert-basis reduction,
394	   * keyed by lambda. Each call to `addCone` appends the cone for the current
395	   * disjunct, and `getStarConstraints` computes the starLia constraints for
396	   * the newly added cones, accumulating them across calls.
397	   */
398	  std::map<Node, std::vector<std::pair<Node, libnormaliz::Cone<Integer>>>>
399	      d_lazyCones;
400	
401	  /**
402	   * The per-cone starLia constraints computed so far for each lambda node
403	   * (`n[0]`). `getStarConstraints` only generates the skolems and constraints
404	   * for cones in `d_lazyCones` that have not been processed yet, appending
405	   * them here, so previously computed constraints (and their skolems) are
406	   * reused across refinement rounds. These are the constraints that are
407	   * independent of the other cones (the (>= mu 0), (>= l 0), and
408	   * (=> (= mu 0) (= l 0)) constraints); the sum constraints span all cones
409	   * and are rebuilt each call.
410	   */
411	  std::map<Node, std::vector<Node>> d_starConstraints;
412	  /**

415	   * constraints over all cones on each call to `getStarConstraints`.
416	   */
417	  std::map<Node, std::vector<std::pair<Vector, std::vector<Vector>>>> d_lambdas;

419	  std::map<Node, size_t> d_processedCones;

423	   * STAR_CONTAINS literal by `lazyHilbert`. The model-value check in

427	  std::map<Node, Node> d_lastStarLia;

436	  std::map<Node, Node> d_lastGuard;

input.reasoning: CONFIRMED real. Independently reproduced: /tmp/liastar_pushpop2.smt2 (same lambda as regress simple.smt2; queries (1 1) then, after pop, (2 1), both genuinely unsat since any nonzero star member has coordinate-sum >= 5) answers unsat then SAT under --arith-liastar-main-solver with build/bin/cvc5 (binary at 06:43 today, newer than all modified sources), while default-lazy subsolver, --arith-liastar-push-pop, and eager modes all answer unsat/unsat. Mechanism verified against code: the guard-chain and driver lemmas are ordinary theory lemmas retracted on user-context pop, but their emission gating is non-context-dependent state: d_mainEnums and d_lastDriver are plain std::map (src/theory/arith/liastar/liastar_extension.h:455,462), and en.guard/en.negated live in MainEnum. getMainEnum returns early for a known lambda (liastar_extension.cpp:828-832) so h_0 => base (line 882) is never re-seeded; the catch-up loop (1060-1070) only emits stages for i >= en.negated so the h_k chain is never re-emitted; emitDriverLemma no-ops when d_lastDriver[literal] == en.guard (1021-1025). In check 2 the only new lemma is the driver for the new literal, literal => (p[2,1] or h_1), where h_1 is a dangling SAT variable with no chain behind it; the SAT solver sets it true with the skolems in the already-covered cell. The -t liastar-ext trace confirms this: check 2 re-harvests the identical disjunct (and (>= (+ x y) 5) (< (+ x (- y)) 6) (>= x 0) (>= y 0)) already coned in check 1, which is only possible if h_1 => not(D_1) was retracted. mainSolverCheckStar then hits the dedupe path (1120-1128), emitDriverLemma no-ops, doPendingLemmas sends nothing, the round ends lemma-free and the bogus model is accepted as sat. The bug is introduced by the new mode: MainEnum and this whole path are new in the diff, and the subsolver modes are immune because their accumulated negations live in the persistent subsolver engine, not the main solver's retractable clause database. The reviewer's note that regress simple.smt2 masks this is also correct: its post-pop vector (4,4) satisfies p directly, so the p[v] split certifies it without the enumeration chain. Fix direction (user-context-dependent gating, e.g. CDO/CDHashMap on userContext(), or re-seeding the chain on user-context change) is sound.
